# jenkins_user (Resource)

Manages a user account in Jenkins' own user database (the local security realm).

Requires the active security realm to be "Jenkins' own user database". On other realms (LDAP, OIDC, ...) operations fail with a clear diagnostic.

All attributes force replacement when changed: in-place updates of a local user's password, full name, or email are not supported, so a change recreates the account. API-token management is out of scope.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "jenkins_user" "developer" {
  username  = "jdoe"
  password  = var.jdoe_password # keep secrets out of source control
  full_name = "Jane Doe"
  email     = "jane.doe@example.com"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `password` (String, Sensitive) The user's password. Stored in state (sensitive) and never read back from Jenkins. Changing it recreates the user.
- `username` (String) The unique login name of the user.

### Optional

- `email` (String) The user's email address. Required when the Mailer plugin is installed (Jenkins rejects account creation without a valid address).
- `full_name` (String) The user's display name. Defaults to the username.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The user ID (same as `username`).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Users are imported by their username. The password is not read back from
# Jenkins, so set it in configuration after importing.
terraform import jenkins_user.developer jdoe
```
